data.name: Rule_MaxDailyWorkingTime_Text
data.value: A working day is capped at 8 hours. It may reach 10 hours if the average over 24 weeks (six months) comes back to 8. A shift longer than that is cut.

data.name: Rule_Breaks_Text
data.value: More than 6 hours of work owe 30 minutes of break, more than 9 hours owe 45, in pieces of at least 15 minutes — and never more than 6 hours in a row without one. Breaks are carved out of the shift; a running operation pauses and resumes.

data.name: Rule_RestPeriod_Text
data.value: Between two working days a crew gets 11 uninterrupted hours of rest (10 in a few named sectors). A shift that would start too soon after the crew's previous one is delayed.

data.name: Rule_NightWork_Text
data.value: A shift with more than 2 hours between 23:00 and 06:00 is night work and is capped at 8 hours (10 with monthly averaging), even where the day cap is 10.

data.name: Rule_SundayRest_Text
data.value: No work from 00:00 to 24:00 on Sundays unless a § 10 exception applies. Multi-shift plants may move that window by up to 6 hours.

data.name: Rule_HolidayRest_Text
data.value: The same ban applies to public holidays. Which days those are is set by the federal state — nine apply everywhere, the rest differ.

data.name: Rule_FreeSundays_Text
data.value: Even where Sunday work is permitted, at least 15 Sundays a year must stay free. A pattern that staffs every Sunday is reported.

data.name: Rule_RestCompensation_Text
data.value: § 5 (2) reserves a rest shortened to 10 hours for hospitals and other institutions for treatment and care, catering and accommodation, transport undertakings, broadcasting, agriculture and animal husbandry — and even there only where every shortening is made good within a calendar month or four weeks by extending another rest to at least 12 hours.

data.name: Rule_MultiShiftRequirement_Text
data.value: The start and end of the Sunday and holiday rest may be moved by up to six hours, forward or back — but only in multi-shift plants running a regular day and night shift. A pattern with only one of the two claims a permission § 9 (2) does not give it.

data.name: Rule_ReplacementRestDay_Text
data.value: § 11 (3) gives a crew that works a Sunday a replacement rest day within a two-week period that includes the Sunday worked; § 11 (2) gives one within eight weeks for work on a public holiday that falls on a working day. The permission to work those days brings the obligation with it.

data.name: Applied_MultiShiftRequirement
data.value: {0}: the Sunday and holiday rest is moved by {2}, which § 9 (2) allows only in a multi-shift plant with a regular day and night shift.

data.name: Applied_ReplacementRestDay
data.value: {0} on {1}: a replacement rest day is owed for it, within {3} (§ 11 (2), (3)).

data.name: Wt_AveragingWindow
data.value: Reference period for the average (§ 3 s. 2)

data.name: Wt_RestNoSector
data.value: Outside the sectors § 5 (2) names there is no entitlement to shorten the rest, so 11 hours is the only value on offer.

data.name: Wt_RestSectorOpened
data.value: A sector is declared, so the shortened rest of 10 hours is now on offer — and with it the duty to compensate.

data.name: Wt_RestCompensationNote
data.value: Every rest shortened this way has to be made good within a calendar month or four weeks by extending another rest of the same crew to at least {0} (§ 5 (2)).

data.name: Wt_SundayRotationHint
data.value: A rota of four weeks means each crew works every fourth Sunday; a rota of one week means the same crew works all of them.

data.name: Wt_SundayRotationOpened
data.value: Sunday work is permitted, so the crew rota now decides how many Sundays stay free.

data.name: Wt_AveragingNote
data.value: § 3 s. 2 allows the ten-hour working day only while the average stays at eight hours per Werktag — Monday to Saturday — across the reference period. § 6 (2) asks the same of night work over four weeks. Both are computed from the pattern above.

data.name: Wt_AveragingNone
data.value: This pattern staffs nobody, so there is no working time to average.
